Stage 3 · Grammar

Grammar

at 3 o'clock · in the morning · at night
PrepositionUseExample
at+ clock timeat 3 o'clock
atnight / middayat night · at midday
in themorning / afternoon / eveningin the morning
It'ssaying the timeIt's half past nine.
  • at + clock time: at 7, at 3 o'clock, at half past six.
  • in the morning / in the afternoon / in the evening.
  • BUT: at night (not “in the night”). Also at midday / at midnight.
  • Ask: What time is it? — It's 3 o'clock. / It's half past nine.

→ Present Simple (I get up, I go home) comes next.

🔧 Build it yourself
  • 🔧 Build it yourself
  • Build it: AT + clock time (at 3 o'clock), IN + part of day (in the morning) — but AT night.
  • ⚠ В 3 часа → AT 3 o'clock (not in!). Утром → IN the morning. Ночью → AT night.

Why these answers

What time is it? → It's + time. at + clock time; in the morning; at night. Half past (:30), quarter to (:45). Numbers: six, nine.

Stage 6 · Speaking

Your turn

Write two short lines about your day with times: at … / in the … .

When you finish, open the model answer and check yourself.

Model answer

I get up at seven in the morning. Lunch is at midday. The film is at eight in the evening. Good night!

Check yourself:

  • Did you use at + a clock time?
  • Did you use in the morning / afternoon / evening?
  • Did you say at night (not “in the night”)?
